text: You just woke up at night with your calf locked up like a rock.
You were sleeping with your toes pointed so your calf was already squeezed short.
That's two big muscles that pull on the thick tendon at your heel.
A nerve runs down into them to tell them when to squeeze.
Each signal makes the tiny fibers inside grab on and pull then let go.
But in a short tired muscle the nerve endings start firing on their own.
Up to one hundred fifty times a second.
The fibers never get a break to let go so the whole muscle locks into a hard knot.
So straighten your leg and pull your toes back toward you.
Stretching the muscle long usually shuts the cramp right off.
It can stay sore for hours and up to six in ten adults get these at night.
